In the common case the omitted commits are old ones that no live milestone's question turns on, so the call stays useful where a refusal would stop the chain, and the stdout line shape is untouched. The omission stays silent wherever stderr is not read. A runner whose fixed call discards or ignores stderr, or that reads only the printed lines, treats a truncated list as complete, for example a finish summary missing tasks or `derive-tasks` taking satisfied work as undone. It also adds a third output kind beside lines and `Error:` (a warning with exit 0) that every caller's prose must know about, and it departs from the draft's stated stop.

alternative.id: Print with a stdout marker line

open-question.alternative: `tasks` runs the shallow check, and in a shallow clone it prints every line the truncated log yields, then one fixed, identifier-free marker line on stdout after them, saying that the record is truncated by a shallow clone. It exits 0. A complete clone prints no marker. With the body flag, the marker follows the last task's body. The warning travels in the very print the reader reasons over, so it cannot be dropped by a redirect, and readers keep a partial record instead of a stop. Whether to proceed on a partial record becomes a decision each reader can make in prose while seeing the gap. It breaks the one-fixed-shape-per-query contract: every line of the print is no longer a task line, so every reader and every parser of the line shape (the "Tasks line fields" and "Tasks body layout" questions' axes) must recognize and skip the marker. A reader that misses it counts it as a task or ignores it. It also departs from the draft's stated stop.

`tasks` makes no shallow check and prints whatever the path-scoped log yields, in a shallow clone and a complete one alike. The limit is stated only in the tool's `--help` text and the docs (and the draft's "Limits to state up front" is revised to match), with no stop line, no warning, and no test. Detection is left to a later milestone, for example the one that adds `summary`, `milestones`, and `record`, whose readers depend on finish commits that a shallow clone would cut just the same, or never if no field run meets the case. It is the smallest birth for the tool. This repository is not shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` prints false), every test builds its own complete fixture repository, and the five readers only enrich their reasoning with the list. Nothing is added that no measured run has needed, and the question can be settled for all history-side queries at once when they land. It leaves the exact failure the question names: in a shallow clone, such as a default CI checkout running a headless chain, older task commits drop out with no sign. Finish's summary or `derive-tasks`' coverage check then reasons from an incomplete record it takes as whole. It also contradicts the draft's written limit until the draft is revised.
